subject: Plotting predict() with scaled covariates but not having the x-axis scaled

messages.author: b063227c9709ab9e
messages.subject: Plotting predict() with scaled covariates but not having the x-axis scaled
parts:
Hi there,

I have been searching this forum for an answer with no luck and have tried various methods to try and correct this issue.

I am trying to plot my predict() outcomes but not have the x-axis in the scaled values.

My code is as follows:

covs <- read.csv("covariates_noNA.csv")
area <- as.matrix(covs[,4]) #is categorical
places <- as.matrix(covs[,5])
boundary <- as.matrix(covs[,6])
river <- as.matrix(covs[,7])
road <- as.matrix(covs[,8])

covs <- data.frame(places, boundary, river, road)

fivedays <- read.csv("detection history 5days.csv")
det5 <- fivedays[,2:40]

#create occupancy object
umf <- unmarkedFrameOccu(y=det5,siteCovs= data.frame(scale(covs),center = TRUE, scale = TRUE, area)) 

Mod30 <- occu(~area+boundary+river+road~road, umf) #top performing model

range(umf@siteCovs$boundary)

#DETECTION INGEI boundary
range(umf@siteCovs$boundary)
ndboundary <- data.frame(boundary=seq(-4.313162,1.960695), river=mean(umf@siteCovs$river), road=mean(umf@siteCovs$road), area=factor("Ingei", levels=c("Andulau","Belalong", "Ingei", "Kiudang", "Labi", "Liang")))

predict.boundary <- predict(Mod30, type="det", newdata=ndboundary, appendData=TRUE)

my_y2 <- expression(paste("Dectection probability (  " , italic(p),")"))
plot2 <- ggplot(predict.boundary, aes(x=boundary, y=Predicted))+ geom_ribbon(aes(ymin=lower, ymax=upper),alpha=0.2) + geom_line(size=1) + ylim(0,1) + theme_classic() + labs(y=my_y2, x="Distance to boundary (m)") + theme(text=element_text(family = "serif",), axis.text.x = element_text(colour="black", size = 12), axis.text.y = element_text(colour = "black", size = 12)) + theme(axis.title = element_text(size = 14))
plot2

Any help will be greatly apprecitated.

Best wishes,
Jess

messages.author: 4f80e1927b0757cb
messages.subject: Re: Plotting predict() with scaled covariates but not having the x-axis scaled
parts:
There are two ways to approach this.

1. Instead of standardizing your covariates ahead of time, have unmarked do the work for you by putting scale() in the formulas, e.g.

occu(~scale(area)~scale(road), umf).

Then when using predict, supply the newdata on the original (non-standardized) covariate scale, and combine the newdata and the results from predict when making the plot.

2. If you standardize the covariates yourself first, as you have done, it's a little harder. After fitting the model, create a covariate range to plot (x), on the original scale. Then standardize this range *using the same values for the mean and SD used to standardize the original dataset*. Supply the standardized range of values x_scaled to the predict newdata argument. Then plot the results of predict (y) vs. the original covariate range (x). If you have other non-focal covariates in the model you are holding constant, you need to standardize them the same way before putting them in the newdata, using the mean and SD values from the original dataset.

Ken
